text.p: PRAVDA - U.S. Ambassador to Bratislava, Ralph Johnson, said Slovakia's exclusion from the first wave of NATO enlargement was a result of political decisions made in Bratislava and not in Washington or Brussels.

- Johnson repeated the main reasons for U.S. concerns over the development of democracy in Slovakia, pointing out exclusion of the opposition from parliamentary control over the secret service, treatment of minorities and failure to investigate serious crimes with political implications.

NARODNA OBRODA - The government is expected to discuss at its regular session on Tuesday unspecified measures aimed at curbing a burgeoning trade deficit with Russia. The preliminary agenda includes no other major economic items.
- Water levels on all Slovak rivers are falling. The only problematic river is the Morava, on the border with the Czech Republic, but no major flooding are expected on the Slovak side.
- Interbank interest rates eased by some eight percent on Monday after the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) indicated that it would continue to add crown liquidity to the local money market.
- Construction company Banske Stavby Prievidza, specialising in mining projects, has started to build a 4,200-kilometre tunnel in northern Syria.
SME - Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) leader Jan Carnogursky said Slovakia would not be integrated into western structures under Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's government.

- The Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) has interrupted the social dialogue with the government, arguing the union was excluded from discussions on crucial issues. KOZ President Ivan Saktor has not ruled out that the unions may prepare a general strike in the autumn.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski has cancelled his visit to Slovakia, planned for July 16 and 17, because of the current flooding in Poland.
- Minister of Agricutlure Peter Baco said about one third of grain could be affected by recent heavy rains. Baco said it was too early to calculate financial damage.
- The European Commission has warned Slovakia that its economy is showing signs of overheating, pointing mainly to a growing current account defcit and rising inflation.
